parts.t: Salmon River covers the rural centre of Langley Township, north of Fraser Highway between Murrayville and Aldergrove, reaching up toward Fort Langley. It is named for the river that runs through it to the Fraser. Large parts sit over the Hopington aquifer and inside the Township’s Salmon River Uplands plan area, so groundwater, creeks and drainage come up on almost every property.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 9, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the Township’s Rural Plan and Water Management Plan, Parks Canada, the Province and the other sources noted on this page. Plans are updated, so confirm what applies to a property with the Township and the Agricultural Land Commission.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Planning and water in Salmon River

parts.t: The Uplands policies and the aquifer decide what can be built. Read what applies before you write an offer.
The Salmon River Uplands section of the Rural Plan was rewritten by Bylaw 5983 on March 11, 2024.
It asks new development to keep natural drainage, protect water flowing into the Salmon River and reduce flooding downstream.
It also calls for a connected trail network and design rules that protect streetscapes and view corridors.
The Water Management Plan reported elevated nitrate in the Hopington aquifer. Septic systems and fertilizer are two common sources.
Fish-bearing streams have setbacks from the top of bank or edge of floodplain, for example 30 m for a Class A watercourse.
